items.title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations
items.content:
Flint-interactive gives AI agents a language for creating interactive visualizations. Click a chart, filter data, highlight related content, and explore beyond the view the author originally chose.

items.title: Proof-based general-purpose computing with Magnetar
items.content:
Zero-knowledge proofs can verify computing results without rerunning workloads or exposing sensitive data. Magnetar helps bring them into the mainstream with support for standard programming languages, major speed gains, and quantum-resistant security.

items.title: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
items.content:
StudentSim is a research system for evaluating and improving AI tutoring tools before they are tested with learners. It models how individuals may engage with tutors, giving feedback to improve tutor performance across subjects like chess, writing, and mathematics.

The post Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring appeared first on Microsoft Research.

items.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
items.content:

items.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
items.content:
Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives.

items.title: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology
items.content:
Biology doesn't operate in silos, and neither should the AI representation of it. Quine is an early-stage research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology. By connecting insights across biological scales and modalities, Quine helps scientists computationally search a space far larger than intuition allows and prioritize hypotheses before they reach the lab. Experimental results provide important feedback, helping researchers sharpen future research directions.

The post Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology appeared first on Microsoft Research.
